# Head injuries and concussion

What the urgent care nurse gave us after the soccer collision.

## Concussion signs

A concussion is a brain injury from a blow or a jolt. Signs: headache, feeling foggy or confused, nausea, dizziness, sensitivity to light and noise, trouble concentrating, and feeling "off". A person does not have to pass out to have a concussion, and symptoms can take hours to show.

## Go to the emergency room if

Go to the emergency department or call 911 if there is loss of consciousness, repeated vomiting, a headache that keeps getting worse, a seizure, slurred speech, weakness or numbness, one pupil larger than the other, clear fluid from the nose or ears, or the person cannot be woken. In a baby, a bulging soft spot or inconsolable crying is also an emergency sign.

## Rest and recovery

Rest for the first 24 to 48 hours, then return to ordinary activity bit by bit as symptoms allow. Limit screens while headaches are bad. Most people feel normal within 2 to 4 weeks, children a little more slowly.

## Back to school and sports

Return to school first, with breaks. Sports come back in steps: light walking, then jogging, then drills, then contact, a day at each step, and only when the person has no symptoms at the previous step and a doctor agrees.

## Bumps in toddlers

A "goose egg" on a toddler's forehead is common. Hold a cold pack on it for 20 minutes, and watch for the next 24 hours for unusual sleepiness, vomiting or crying that will not settle.
